identity.title: Genomic characterization of Pediococcus acidilactici AB01 isolated from Algerian Targui camel milk: insights into safety, probiotic-associated traits, and functional potential.

content.abstract: Pediococcus acidilactici displays substantial strain-level variation, requiring genome-resolved evaluation of new food-associated isolates. This study characterized P. acidilactici AB01, isolated from raw milk of Algerian Targui camels, and used previously generated in vitro observations only to contextualize genomic predictions. Illumina sequencing yielded a 2,117,438-bp draft genome with 42.0% GC content, 36 contigs, and an N50 of 389,234 bp. BUSCO recovered 99.2% complete markers, whereas CheckM estimated 98.23% completeness and 2.43% contamination. ANIb values calculated with IPGA were 99.01% and 98.71% relative to the P. acidilactici type-strain deposits DSM 20,284(T) and JCM 8797(T), respectively; dDDH values of 91.2% supported species assignment. ResFinder detected no known acquired antimicrobial-resistance genes, and no virulence-factor match satisfied the predefined identity and reference-coverage criteria. CARD-RGI additionally identified three distant Strict homolog matches (sdrM-like, qacG-like, and alr/vanT-like), which were examined according to their sequence characteristics and genomic contexts. Functional annotation identified candidate genetic determinants potentially associated with stress responses, carbohydrate metabolism, and cell-surface interactions, together with a predicted Type II-A CRISPR-Cas locus containing 29 spacers with putative viral matches. Comparative analysis of 85 P. acidilactici genomes identified an open pan-genome comprising 5,485 clusters (Heaps-law gamma = 0.266). Seventy-seven candidate clusters occurred only in AB01 within this dataset, of which 67 remained after excluding clusters containing partial coding-sequence annotations. Overall, these findings highlight the genomic diversity of P. acidilactici and identify AB01 as a promising candidate requiring further in-depth experimental evaluation before its safety and probiotic, biopreservative, or functional potential can be established.
